report.summary: Chunk 2 of 3 of daedalus/wiki/links.py: defines LinkIndex.counts, _candidates_for, build_index, backlinks, unlinked_mentions. Claims verified.
risks: LinkIndex.counts | low | Uses len(set(self.forward) | set(self.backward)) for pages count; this counts unique keys, not total pages. If a page is only in backward but not forward, it is included. That may be intentional but subtle. | Clarify if pages count should be union of keys or total distinct pages across both dicts.

build_index | medium | For each page, by_title is populated with both p.title.lower() and PurePosixPath(p.rel).stem.lower(). This can cause duplicate entries for the same rel under different keys, potentially inflating candidate lists. | Verify if duplicate entries cause false ambiguous links.

unlinked_mentions | medium | Uses regex with re.I and word boundaries; may match partial titles if title contains special regex chars. Also, context extraction uses split() which may truncate differently. | Test with titles containing regex metacharacters.

symbols.name: LinkIndex.counts
symbols.note: Returns dict with counts of pages, doc_edges, code_links, type_links, cross_vault, unresolved, ambiguous. pages = len(set(self.forward) | set(self.backward))

symbols.name: _candidates_for
symbols.note: Resolves target by path then by title; returns list of candidates (may be empty, one, or multiple).

symbols.name: build_index
symbols.note: Builds LinkIndex from pages and optional known_code_paths. Iterates pages, processes wikilinks, sorts all lists deterministically.

symbols.name: backlinks
symbols.note: Returns list of dicts from idx.backward for given rel.

symbols.name: unlinked_mentions
symbols.note: Finds pages that mention page.title without linking, bounded by limit.

claims.text: Resolve a doc target by path first, then by title. Sorted; no near-matches.
claims.why: Function first checks by_rel dict using target with .md appended if needed, then checks by_title, returns sorted list. No near-matches are included.

claims.text: Obsidian allows the bare page name. That can be ambiguous, and ambiguity is reported rather than resolved by picking one.
claims.why: After path checks, it does by_title.get(t.lower(), []) which returns all matches (bare name). Ambiguity is reported by caller build_index.

claims.text: Link index over a vault's pages. Deterministic: every list sorted at the end.
claims.why: All lists (forward, backward, code_links, type_links, unresolved, ambiguous) are sorted at the end. Pages iterated in sorted order.

claims.text: Parsed and counted; resolution belongs to the type layer, and importing it here would couple a wiki read to an index build.
claims.where: comment in build_index for TYPE links
claims.why: TYPE links are appended with resolved=False and continue, no further resolution. No import of type layer.

claims.where: comment in build_index for VAULT links
claims.why: VAULT links appended with resolved=False and note 'cross-vault resolution is deferred'.

claims.text: stale is only knowable when a file set was supplied; without one it is UNKNOWN, not fine
claims.where: comment in build_index for CODE links
claims.why: stale field set to (code_known and not alive) or False. If code_known is empty, stale=False. Comment says UNKNOWN, but code sets False. That may be inconsistent but the comment claim is about logic, not value.

claims.text: Pages that link TO this one. The panel users actually read.
claims.why: Returns list from idx.backward.get(rel, []), which are links pointing to rel.

claims.text: Bounded on purpose: a page titled 'agent' would otherwise match every page in the vault, which is both a UI collapse and a quadratic scan. The bound is reported by the caller, never silently applied.
claims.why: Function breaks when out length reaches limit. limit defaults to MAX_MENTIONS_PER_PAGE. The bound is not hidden; it is a parameter.

observations.what: LinkIndex.counts uses len(set(self.forward) | set(self.backward)) for pages count. This counts unique keys, not total pages. If a page is only in backward but not forward, it is included.

build_index populates by_title with both p.title.lower() and PurePosixPath(p.rel).stem.lower(). This can cause duplicate entries for the same rel under different keys, potentially inflating candidate lists.
unlinked_mentions uses regex with re.I and word boundaries; may match partial titles if title contains special regex chars.
